item.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s. We also discuss the connections between this filtration and triply-graded link homology.
item.dc:creator: Joshua P. Turner

item.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
item.description: arXiv:2611.28761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over commutative Noetherian rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over every commutative Noetherian ring.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Hua, Shun-Jie Li, Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.
item.dc:creator: Toshinori Kobayashi, Yuki Mifune

item.title: Homological Properties of $L\otimes_{\Bbbk} N$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian algebras over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ such that $A\otimes_\Bbbk B$ is Noetherian. Let $I$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$ and $B$, respectively, and let $L$ and $N$ be nonzero finitely generated modules over $A$ and $B$, respectively. In \cite{R4}, the author investigates the relationships between certain algebraic properties of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ and the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$, and vice versa. In the present paper, we characterize the Gorensteinness, approximate Cohen--Macaulayness, and maximal depth property of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ with respect to $\mathcal{I}=I\otimes_\Bbbk B+A\otimes_\Bbbk J$ in terms of the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$ with respect to $I$ and $J$, respectively. In particular, when $A$ and $B$ are local rings, we describe these properties of $L \otimes_{\Bbbk} N$ as a module over the local ring $A \otimes_\Bbbk B$.
item.dc:creator: Ahad Rahimi

item.title: Comparable Overrings of Marot Rings II
item.description: arXiv:2611.29325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a Marot ring. We study comparable overrings of $R$ that are integral over $R$, generalizing results of Ayache for integral domains. We show that such an overring has at most two regular maximal ideals. When $R$ has a unique regular maximal ideal, we study the three possible types and give characterizations of comparability and minimality in the first two cases. In the case of two regular maximal ideals, we describe the integral closure of $R$ as an intersection of two valuation overrings. We also obtain comparability criteria using normal pairs and finite chain conditions. Finally, we construct counterexamples giving negative answers to two conjectures posed by Ayache.
item.dc:creator: Ba\c{s}ak Ay Saylam, Eren Canan

item.title: Some results on the isotropy groups of non-invertible simple derivations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $2\le i<n$, and let $d_i$ be a $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots,x_i]$. We study the $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ of the form $d_n=d_i+\sum_{j=i}^{n-1}\bigl(a_jx_{j+1}+g_j(x_j)\bigr)\partial_{x_{j+1}}$ where $a_j\in k$ and $g_j\in k[x_j]\setminus k$. Under suitable conditions on $d_i$, we show that the isotropy group of $d_n$ consists of translations and is either trivial or isomorphic to $(k,+)$.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Chandra Mishra, Dibyendu Mondal, Pankaj Shukla, Sneha Singh

item.title: Regular models for F-coherent rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.30705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ with perfection $R^\infty$. We study whether coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R^\infty\cong S^\infty$ for some regular Noetherian local ring $S$. For a normal Noetherian local domain, coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R$ to be $p$-almost factorial, equivalently $R^\infty$ is a GCD domain; a finite regular extension $R\subseteq S$ with $S^q\subseteq R$ gives the uniform bound $q Cl(R)=0$. In the non-Noetherian direction, we construct, for every prime $p$ and every $d\geq2$, a perfect coherent local valuation domain of dimension $d$ that is not the perfection of any Noetherian ring. In the positive direction, we characterize coherence for affine semigroup local rings. Finally, we give an F-coherent ring without regular model.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: Standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart rings have unimodal $h$-vectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.31151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the $h$-vector $(h_0,\ldots,h_s)$ of every standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart ring is unimodal, with a peak at position $\lceil s/2\rceil$. More generally, a standard graded Ehrhart ring has an alternatingly increasing $h$-vector if the radical of the ideal generated by the degree-one part of its canonical trace ideal contains the homogeneous maximal ideal. In characteristic zero or two, the generic Artinian reduction of each such ring has the strong Lefschetz property. We also prove unimodality for every standard graded nearly Gorenstein domain of dimension at least two with $h$-vector $(1,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, where $s\geq2$, provided that $h_1-h_s\leq1$. In the level case this $h$-vector is both concave and alternatingly increasing. If $h_1=h_s$, then $h_1=\cdots=h_s$.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Sora Miyashita

item.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.
item.dc:creator: Jinbang Yang

item.title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form $\mathcal{H}_\rho(K)$: a valued field $K$ read up to relative error $\rho$. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient $K^\times/T\cup\{0\}$ of a field, the norm axiom forces $T=1+\mathfrak{m}_\rho$ for a valuation on $K$. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group $\mathbb{Z}$ we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Linzi

item.title: Higher Coherence of Flat Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.29508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish higher-coherence results for flat algebras over commutative base rings. If $K$ is noetherian and a $K$-flat algebra $A$ admits an $A^{\mathrm e}$-resolution of length $n$ with projective term in degree $n$ and flat terms in lower degrees, then every product of copies of $A$ has right flat dimension at most $n-1$ and $A$ is left strongly $n$-coherent. A projective $n$-th relative bar syzygy gives the corresponding two-sided conclusion. If $K$ is coherent and $A$ is $K$-flat and relatively quasi-free, then $A$ is left and right strongly $2$-coherent. In contrast, we construct a countable commutative ring $k$ that is strongly $n$-coherent for every $n\ge2$, while the one-variable polynomial algebra $k[z]$ is faithfully flat and relatively quasi-free over $k$ but fails strong $q$-coherence for every finite $q$. Explicit modules witness failure at each positive degree. These results establish coherence transfer over coherent bases and show that the analogous higher-degree transfer fails for every $n\ge2$, even after any fixed finite shift.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pavlov, Mikhail Dusman

item.title: Kato-Milne cohomology over rational function fields in characteristic p>0
item.description: arXiv:2611.29511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. In this note, we describe the Kato-Milne cohomology of the rational function field F(x) in one variable x over F. In particular, we extend the Milnor-Scharlau exact sequence [12, Theorem 5.2] to characteristic p. As an application of this exact sequence, we further obtain the norm theorem [16, Theorem A.3] in characteristic p.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Laghribi, Trisha Maiti

item.title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
item.description: arXiv:2611.29782v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem. We develop Gr\"obner bases for ideals of the free algebra and prove that the elements $e_k\oplus\tau$, with $\tau$ ranging over any set of permutations, form a Gr\"obner basis for the lexicographic ordering and for its opposite. This gives an algebraic form of the theorem of Backelin, West and Xin: the permutations avoiding all $k\cdots21\oplus\tau$ and those avoiding all $12\cdots k\oplus\tau$ are two monomial bases of one and the same quotient.
item.dc:creator: Anton Khoroshkin

item.title: Partition rank and analytic rank over finite field
item.description: arXiv:2611.30721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the partition rank and the analytic rank of a tensor over any finite field are equivalent up to a constant depending only on the order of the tensor. The proof combines Mili\'cevi\'c's theorem on dense multilinear varieties with the differential Schur complement of Moshkovitz and Zhu. The new ingredient is a method for approximately eliminating multilinear equations.
item.dc:creator: Qiyuan Chen, Ke Ye

item.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.30790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.
item.dc:creator: Hoang Le Truong

item.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded commutative algebras
item.description: arXiv:2511.07937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We call a standard graded commutative $\Bbbk$-algebra \textit{cyclotomic} if its $h$-polynomial has all its roots on the unit circle in the complex plane. Complete intersections provide typical examples of cyclotomic algebras, since the $h$-polynomial of any standard graded complete intersection is a product of polynomials of the form $1 + t + \cdots + t^{m-1}$. We refer to such polynomials as being \textit{of type CI}. A natural question is whether there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra whose $h$-polynomial is not of type CI. In this paper, we give a partial answer to this question. We show that the $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ of a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ is of type CI whenever $h_R(1) \in \{1, 4, 6\}$ or $h_R(1)$ is prime. On the other hand, if $n$ is a composite integer with $n \geq 8$, then there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ whose $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ is not of type CI and satisfies $h_R(1) = n$.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Higashitani, Kenta Ueyama

item.title: A Weaker Notion of Atomicity in Integral Domains
item.description: arXiv:2512.08850v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A nonzero element of an integral domain $D$ is called \emph{atomic} if it is a unit or can be written as a finite product of irreducible elements of $D$, and $D$ is called \emph{atomic} if every nonzero element of $D$ is atomic. Here, we introduce and study a weaker notion of atomicity, which relaxes the requirement that all elements admit a factorization into irreducibles. Namely, we say that an integral domain is \emph{sub-atomic} if every divisor of an atomic element is also atomic. Then, we investigate the basic properties of such domains, provide examples, and explore the behavior of the sub-atomic property under standard constructions such as localization and $D+M$ constructions. In particular, we prove that the sub-atomic property ascends to polynomial rings in the class of GL-domains. Our results highlight the independence of the sub-atomic property from other classical factorization properties, and it forms an important class of integral domains lying between atomic and antimatter domains (i.e., domains without atoms).
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Benelmekki, Brahim Boulayat

item.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.03208v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.
item.dc:creator: Timo Sch\"urg

item.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.
item.dc:creator: Guocheng Dai, Jiangsheng Hu

item.title: Seshadri Regions and the Asymptotic Shape of Multigraded Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2512.05289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the Seshadri region of a subvariety, a convex region packaging the classical Seshadri constants with respect to every line bundle simultaneously. We develop the theory of Seshadri regions as a measure of positivity along subvarieties and apply it to determine asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for ideal powers and symmetric powers on smooth projective toric varieties.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Bruce, Lauren Cranton Heller, Mahrud Sayrafi, Alexandra Seceleanu
